## Highlights

**GitHub App tokens in both current formats are now detected.** The new signature rule `github-user-to-server-token` reports GitHub App user-to-server tokens (`ghu_` prefix). `github-app-token` now also reads the stateless installation token format, `ghs_` followed by a numeric app ID, `_` and three dot-separated base64url segments, beside the older `ghs_` form.

**Dense lines no longer slow the scan down.** A long line holding thousands of candidates used to take time quadratic in its length. One `redact-claude` payload line of 64000 URLs with passwords took 51 to 64 seconds; it now takes 0.3 seconds. Findings are unchanged.

**Placeholder words and documentation paths hide fewer real credentials.** Built-in stopwords such as `test` or `fake` no longer match inside an opaque value at a `+`, `/` or `=`, and credential-anchored rules no longer get a lower entropy bar in README and docs files.

**`http-basic-auth` stops reporting prose.** A value after `Basic` is now reported only when it decodes as HTTP Basic credentials, so most phrases such as `Basic word/word/word` in text and code are now clear.

**Named-key values stay on their own line.** In agent output, `generic-token-assignment`, `generic-api-key` and `generic-secret-assignment` no longer read a quoted value across a line break, and a value made only of shell expansions such as `${ID:0:8}` is no longer reported.

## Upgrade notes

- `github-user-to-server-token` is on by default, so a commit that adds such a token is now blocked and agent output that holds one is masked. To turn it off, set `"github-user-to-server-token" = false` under `[settings.rules]`.
- Some values in README and docs files that were previously below the entropy threshold are now reported, because the built-in credential-anchored rules no longer add the documentation entropy bonus. A documented example that is really a placeholder can be cleared with a per-rule allowlist `regexes` entry.
- A hook call whose working directory no longer exists now fails closed when a `.sekretbarilo.toml` lies between the nearest surviving parent directory and your home directory. `redact-claude` masks that output and `check-codex` exits 2. In practice, a command such as `git worktree remove` run from inside the worktree it removes has its output masked once. Later calls from an existing directory behave as before.

Upgrade: `brew upgrade vshuraeff/tap/sekretbarilo`, then `sekretbarilo doctor`.

## Changes

### Detection

- New rule `github-user-to-server-token`, signature class and enabled by default: `ghu_` followed by at least 36 letters and digits.
- `github-app-token` accepts the stateless installation token: `ghs_`, a numeric app ID, `_`, then three base64url segments of at least ten characters joined by dots. The older `ghs_` plus 36 or more letters and digits is still reported. Matching is structural; signatures are not checked.
- `http-basic-auth` keeps a value only when it is standard base64, with `=` padding optional but complete when present, and decodes to bytes that contain a `:` and no ASCII control byte. Any byte from 0x80 up is accepted, so credentials in ISO-8859-1, Windows-1251 or UTF-8 stay reported, and the user name may be empty.
- Known limitation: some slash-joined prose also decodes to bytes that pass these checks. In a generated dictionary sample, about 0.13% of lowercase word pairs and triples, 1.1% of mixed-case pairs and 1.2% to 1.35% of capitalized pairs and triples were still reported. These rates describe that sample, not prose in general.
- `generic-token-assignment`, `generic-api-key` and `generic-secret-assignment`:
  - A quoted value never spans a line break. Before, a quoted token assignment in one line of agent output could run on into the next line, so the scan reported text that was no credential and missed the value that followed. Per-file checks already read one line at a time.
  - A quote right after the separator that closes the string literal holding the name itself, as in a call argument that is just a token-equals string concatenated with a variable, opens no value. The scan resumes behind that quote, so a real assignment later on the line is still found.
  - A value made only of `${...}` shell expansions and at most four separator characters in total is skipped. A literal beside or inside an expansion, such as an opaque default, is still reported.
- `generic-password-assignment`: an unquoted value ends at a `\n`, `\r` or `\t` escape, so two passwords in JSON-printed output are two findings instead of one that spans both values and the name between them.

### Stopwords and documentation files

- The built-in stopword list matches a placeholder word only at a boundary: the value edges, or any punctuation or whitespace other than `+`, `/` and `=`. `[example-token-…]`, `test:…` and `#dummy#…` still read as placeholders, while `/test+` or `.fake/` inside an opaque base64 value no longer hides it.
- For the rules that use the built-in list, a run of `x` or `X` counts as a placeholder only when it fills a whole component of at least three characters, not when it occurs inside a longer random run.
- Built-in rules whose entropy check is anchored by a credential name, an authentication header or a provider format no longer get the +1.0 entropy bonus on documentation paths. A credential is not less sensitive in a README.
- Your own `[allowlist] stopwords` match as before.

### Rule configuration

- New optional per-rule fields describe behaviour that used to be hard-coded for single rules:
  - `builtin_stopwords` (default `true`): `false` checks only your own stopwords.
  - `doc_entropy_bonus` (default `true`): `false` applies the same entropy threshold on documentation paths.
  - `skip_template_lines` (default `true`): `false` keeps reporting on a line with template syntax.
  - `resume_at_value_end` (default `false`): `true` resumes the scan at the end of the secret value instead of the whole match.
  - `base64_credential` (default `false`): `true` keeps a value only when it decodes as HTTP Basic credentials, as described above. `http-basic-auth` sets it.
- A `[[rules]]` override with the id of a built-in rule that leaves out one of these fields keeps the built-in value. A new rule id gets the defaults.
- `wireguard-key-assignment` now sets its behaviour through these fields; its detection is unchanged.

### Performance

- Whole-line checks run once per line instead of once per candidate: the template-line skip, the hash-context words, the import-line and public-key checks, and the quote state used to end a quoted value.
- One line of N URLs with passwords through `redact-claude`:

  | N | 0.12.2 | 0.13.0 |
  | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | 8000 | 1.1 s | 0.09 s |
  | 32000 | 13 to 14 s | 0.19 s |
  | 64000 | 51 to 64 s | 0.31 s |

- Other dense lines of 32000 candidates: assignments 25.3 s to 0.54 s, `["API_KEY=…", …]` lists 25.5 s to 0.67 s, hex values beside `commit` 17.3 s to 0.32 s.

### Agent hooks

- A vanished working directory loads only the fixed system and user configuration layers. The load fails closed when the nearest surviving parent's hierarchy, or the path itself if it reappears, yields any other layer. Before, a removed symlink could make the hook trust a committed allowlist that the live path never read. This applies to `redact-claude` and both `check-codex` events.

### Documentation

- The getting-started scan examples show real masked output and no longer show a success line for a clean scan, which prints nothing.
- Installation troubleshooting checks `core.hooksPath` in every scope instead of an undefined variable.
- The configuration page states the trust limit for committed layers when a hook runs inside a nested repository.
- ADR 0005 records the decision not to build persistent known-value redaction for now and the evidence that would reopen it.

### Tests

- New regression tests for dense lines, GitHub App tokens, Basic credentials, stopword recall and named-key values.
- An ignored measurement test reports how many generated values each entropy-gated rule loses to built-in stopwords and the documentation bonus: `cargo test --test stopword_measurements -- --ignored --nocapture`.
- Smaller test hygiene fixes in the parser-posture and `redact-claude` tests.

### Counts

- 116 built-in rules, 112 of them enabled by default. 76 rules are signature rules and 39 are contextual.
